newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks trail Dow higher at open.

text.p: Australian shares trailed Wall Street higher on Tuesday with rises across the board.
The All Ordinaries index added 11.5 points to 2,494.1.
Mining leaders had the best of it in early trading after metal prices strengthened, but buying interest was widespread.
"Wall Street gave us the lead and we have seen buying across the board," said a Sydney broker, cautioning that the market may not hold its early gains.
"The miners got a good start again but now we have to wait and see if it holds this afternoon," the broker said.

Among the standouts was Victorian regional bank and oft-suggested takeover target Bank of Melbourne, whose shares were sparked by reports of comments from St George Bank that it was still interested in acquisitions, despite having just merged with Advance Bank. Bank of Melbourne sharesp jumped 2.7 percent to an intraday high of A$8.30 (US$6.45).

Biotechnology group Biota Holdings extended Monday's gains, jumping 51 cents to an intraday high of A$4.61 as traders bought in after Monday's announcement that Australian trials of its anti-influenza treatment, Zanamivir, would start in May.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to one, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
